parallel.requirements: Recognized the need for pure ESM .mjs output, no external dependencies, a manual argv parser, safe_load behavior, and PyYAML folded-style dump parity.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent chose three subagents: parser/resolver, emitter, and CLI/entry, with distinct file ownership and an intended later integration/verification phase.
parallel.implementation: CLI child completed argparse.mjs and test15.mjs; parser child wrote only yamlResolver.mjs; emitter child wrote yamlEmitterAnalysis.mjs and yamlEmitter.mjs near the timeout.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Files were written directly into /output, but the parent did not perform a final assembly pass; the artifact list lacks yamlParser.mjs even though test15.mjs imports it.
parallel.verification: CLI behavior was verified by the CLI child; emitter and parser were not end-to-end verified together, and the parent ran no post-swarm integrated test.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Two required child scopes were aborted, the parser entry module was missing, and the official evaluator passed 0/152 samples.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same YAML migration requirements and spent the run mapping PyYAML parsing and dumping semantics from the executable.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Kept all probing, implementation planning, and eventual coding under the single main agent with no subagents or delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial trajectory remained in exploratory probe and design reasoning through its last semantic event and did not write the required .mjs implementation files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No deliverable was assembled or copied from the serial run; status artifact_validation shows an empty files list.
serial.verification: The serial run verified reference behavior through many executable probes, but never verified a JavaScript implementation because none was written.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The single main agent timed out while still preparing to code, leaving no output artifact and 0/152 official tests passed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required ESM files, manual CLI parsing, safe_load, folded dump output, and no dependencies before delegating.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt requirements and independently probed the same PyYAML behavior from the executable.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly similar; the practical difference was that parallel spread requirements across children while serial kept them in one context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assigned parser, emitter, and CLI/entry to separate subagents with nominally distinct file ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had a single owner for all research and intended implementation, with no delegation and no subagent activity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel produced partial components from separate owners; serial avoided coordination boundaries but never moved from research into implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel established a cross-module contract: safeLoad from yamlParser.mjs, dumpFolded from yamlEmitter.mjs, and parseArgs from argparse.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept parser, emitter, CLI, and behavioral findings in one main context, avoiding cross-agent interface handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel contract itself was clear, but it depended on all children returning; the serial run had no inter-agent interface risk but also no written module boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel created /output/test15.mjs, argparse.mjs, yamlResolver.mjs, yamlEmitterAnalysis.mjs, and yamlEmitter.mjs, but no yamlParser.mjs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created no output files; it remained in probe scripts and reference-output analysis.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a partial implementation artifact that could not import its parser; serial had no implementation artifact at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The swarm returned only at cancellation with one completed child and two aborted children; the parent did not resume or process the incomplete results.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results to join; the single main serial turn was cancelled while still active.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed child-result lifecycle around unfinished delegated work, while serial had a simple unfinished single-agent lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote directly into the shared /output tree under non-overlapping file ownership, but the final tree was incomplete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not write shared deliverables, so there was no shared-state collision or integration artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had direct shared-tree writes without a final parent integration pass; serial had no shared output state to integrate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified CLI parsing and syntax locally but had no whole-program smoke test after parser and emitter work; official evaluation passed 0/152.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified many reference executable outputs but never verified a JS implementation; official evaluation also passed 0/152.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel performed component verification for CLI only; serial performed reference probing only. Neither had integrated acceptance evidence.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used a swarm for about the full cell budget, then cancelled the parent and two children after a long unmonitored wait.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the full budget in one long analysis trajectory and was cancelled before implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel budget was spent across concurrent component owners and ended with aborted children; serial budget was spent sequentially on exploration and ended without code.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is not a discordant official outcome: both current completed evaluations failed with 0/152. The concrete task-solving difference is that the parallel run produced a partial multi-file artifact with a missing parser module after an unmonitored swarm timeout, while the serial run produced no artifact because the single agent stayed in reference-behavior probing until cancellation.
parallel_contributors: The parent waited on AgentSwarm until cancellation and did not inspect or reassign partial child work before closure.
The parser child never delivered yamlParser.mjs, so the entry point imported a missing required module.
serial_contributors: The serial agent spent the full budget on black-box probing and implementation planning.
No serial output files were delivered, leaving artifact_validation.files empty.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel had a partial deliverable with CLI and emitter/resolver pieces; serial had no deliverable files.
Neither run reached an integrated JavaScript implementation that could satisfy PyYAML safe_load and dump parity.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Both failed, so the retained pattern is a realized parallel-side adverse process pattern rather than an outcome-differential root cause.

candidates.reason: Parallel assigned implementation ownership to parser, emitter, and CLI children; the failure was unfinished delegated work, not absence of implementation owners.
The parent planned to handle integration after child completion; the problem was that it never monitored or reached that phase.
CLI/entry assembly was explicitly assigned and partly completed; missing parser came from unfinished child work rather than an unowned deliverable.
The parent retained the end-to-end orchestration role; the observed defect is waiting without monitoring, not lack of a named pipeline owner.
Parallel implementation work was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; all three children ran concurrently.
Parallel did not complete all investigation before implementation; children probed and wrote files concurrently.
The critical parser path was active, not starved of an owner; the retained issue is that the parent did not monitor and redirect the running swarm before timeout.
There were only three scoped children, and the evidence points to an unmonitored wait on their progress rather than excessive breadth or repeated retries exhausting budget.
Parser and emitter scopes were broad, but the same timeout chain is better captured by the parent's lack of monitoring or intervention while partial artifacts were visible.
The child briefs included the key task, environment, interface, and delivery requirements; no child failure is traced to a known omitted requirement.
The parent gave explicit exports and import paths for safeLoad, dumpFolded, parseArgs, and test15.mjs; no incompatible returned modules were shown.
No known finding is shown disappearing between actors; the parent simply did not consume results before timeout.
The parent received the large swarm result only at cancellation, so there was no observed decision window where bulk caused non-consumption.
No actor is shown consuming outdated workspace or requirement information; the issue is absent monitoring rather than stale information use.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts were left unadjudicated; the returned result instead says two children were aborted.
The parallel parent did not present the whole task as complete; the run was cancelled and the artifact was later evaluated externally.
No replacement or retry child was launched, so no retry repeated work without inherited checkpoints.
